attributes.goods_price_belief: BELIEF: With accelerating consumer prices and macroeconomic signals pointing to a deliberate economic cooling, I perceive a rising urgency to secure essential goods before further price increases erode purchasing power. As a low-income retiree dependent on asset returns, my consumption will remain focused on necessities. Luxury goods remain out of reach, and the absence of additional subsidies or loan access limits flexibility. Given economic uncertainty and tightening credit, I anticipate continued price pressures on necessities, prompting cautious and constrained spending to safeguard basic needs.
attributes.stock_price_belief: BELIEF: Given the current economic environment of deliberate cooling, rising consumer prices, and slowing domestic demand, the household perceives that stock prices, particularly for necessity stocks, may face downward pressure due to weaker profit rates and economic uncertainty. Luxury stocks, while benefiting from higher profit rates, may also encounter headwinds as the broader economic moderation impacts consumer sentiment and discretionary spending. The household anticipates a cautious or declining trend in stock prices in the short term, prioritizing risk-averse asset management.
attributes.deposit_rate_belief: BELIEF: Given the economic slowdown, deliberate policy-induced cooling, and accelerating consumer prices, we believe deposit interest rates are unlikely to rise significantly in the near term. The central bank appears focused on managing inflation and moderating growth rather than stimulating demand, suggesting deposit rates will remain steady or only marginally adjust. With our low wealth level and reliance on asset returns, maintaining savings in deposits at the current rate seems prudent for stability amidst economic uncertainty.
